title: Portrait of Natsume Soseki (夏目漱石), photographed September/October 1912
sourceCollection: Wikimedia Commons, reproduced from National Diet Library digitized volume 'Soseki Zenshu, Vol. 8' (漱石全集. 第8巻, 1929)
licenseBasis: Photographer Ogawa Kazumasa (小川一真, 1860–1929); photograph taken 1912, published in a 1929 volume. PD in Japan (photographic works published before 1957/pre-1899 Copyright Act provisions; Ogawa died 1929, well past any personal-authorship term) and PD in the US (published before 1929 cutoff under URAA rules applied by Commons). Note: a near-duplicate/related capture from the same 1912 sitting is also on Commons as File:NATSUME_Soseki.jpg (823x1201, from 'Soseki no Omoide', 1928) with the same PD basis — not downloaded, kept as a documented alternate.
notes: Standard formal portrait; commonly identified as the type of photograph on which the old 1000-yen banknote engraving was based, though Commons does not explicitly document banknote-engraving provenance. Treat the 'basis for the 1000 yen note' claim as UNCONFIRMED — the note portrait itself is a separate engraved/stylized artwork (see rejected candidate below).

title: Calligraphy of Natsume Soseki — five-character kanshi (Chinese quatrain) with artist's seal, 1912 (Meiji 45)
sourceCollection: Wikimedia Commons (privately owned original; photographic reproduction uploaded to Commons)
licenseBasis: Author Natsume Soseki, died 1916 → PD in Japan (50 years p.m.a. under the pre-2018 term that governed this work) and in the US.
notes: This is autograph brushwork (漢詩自筆) bearing his 漱石 seal, not a separate cursive pen 'signature' in the Western sense — closest available Commons asset to item 2 (署名/落款). Resolution is modest (320x1089); no higher-resolution version was found on Commons for this specific work.

title: Manuscript page of『吾輩は猫である』(I Am a Cat)
sourceCollection: Wikimedia Commons, reproduced from National Diet Library Digital Collections — 1936 'Soseki Zenshu' (漱石全集) published by Soseki Zenshu Kankokai
licenseBasis: Author Natsume Soseki, died 1916; work published in facsimile before 1931 → PD in Japan and US per Commons PD Mark rationale.
notes: Task asked for a『こゝろ』manuscript page or letter/kanshi specifically; no dedicated Kokoro autograph-manuscript file was located on Commons or via general NDL search in the time available. This is a confirmed, cleanly licensed Soseki autograph manuscript page (different novel) used as the closest verified substitute — flag for maintainer decision on whether a Kokoro-specific manuscript search (direct NDL Digital Collections browse of 漱石全集 volumes, e.g. https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1883350) should be pursued separately.

title: "I Am a Cat" (吾輩ハ猫デアル), English-edition binding/cover design by Hashiguchi Goyo, translated by K. Ando, 1906
sourceCollection: Wikimedia Commons, digitized from Yale University Beinecke Rare Book & Manuscript Library
licenseBasis: Designer Hashiguchi Goyo (橋口五葉), died 1921 → PD (published before 1931, and >50/70 years p.m.a. in Japan).
notes: Task asked specifically for the 1905 Japanese first-edition binding by Hashiguchi Goyo (大倉書店/服部書店 edition). No Commons file was found that is explicitly documented as that exact 1905 first printing; this is a 1906 English-translation edition that reuses/adapts Goyo's cover treatment for the same title, high resolution, confirmed PD. Treat as a documented substitute, not the exact requested artifact — a maintainer should check NDL Digital Collections directly (e.g. dl.ndl.go.jp holdings for 大倉書店 1905 吾輩ハ猫デアル) for the precise first edition if that distinction matters for the art pass.

title: Book cover, first edition of『こゝろ』(Kokoro), 1914 — self-designed binding by Natsume Soseki
sourceCollection: Wikimedia Commons (source listed on file page only as 'Katalog', i.e. an auction/library catalog scan)
licenseBasis: Soseki designed his own binding for Kokoro (1914) and died in 1916 → PD in Japan (50 years p.m.a.) and US.
notes: Low resolution (266x343) — well below the 'high-res 우선' preference in the brief.
